turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Priya, come through. Let your husband wait on the chair outside, I'll call him later. I checked the pressure, it is 108 over 72, and the pulse is 88.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Um, I'm very nervous. I don't know what they'll say.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the previous consult ran over. I'm Dr Iyer. Forget the slip for a minute and tell me what's been happening, in your own time.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, I think I'm pregnant. The home kit was positive, around two weeks ago. And now there is spotting, brownish, only on the liner, very little.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did that spotting start?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days. Or three. I didn't write it down, I don't know, doctor, and it is not there all the time.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the cramping?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Low in the stomach, like period pain. Mild. It comes a few times in the day and then goes.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Last period, even a rough idea?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Around Diwali. Or after Diwali, I'm not sure which. I don't know the date, and my cycles were a bit irregular anyway, so I never tracked properly.

[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): If someone forces around Diwali, the guess lands near eight to ten weeks, but I am not writing a firm number of weeks from that. The scan can date it better than my arithmetic.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): My mother-in-law calls every night, which week, beta, which week. I just keep saying I don't know.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): She'll survive the suspense. Have you had any fever? Any burning or pain while passing urine?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. And no burning. Urine is normal.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any clots, or pieces that looked like tissue?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't think so. Just a few brown drops. I keep thinking the baby is in danger and I can't switch it off.

[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am not going to call this a miscarriage from the story alone. It may be a threatened miscarriage, it may be an ectopic pregnancy we cannot exclude yet, or it may simply be early spotting that settles. I won't choose among those until the scan and the hormone result are here.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Ectopic is the outside-the-womb one, yes? A girl in my office had it. Now my hands are cold.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's the meaning, yes, and I'm naming it so it isn't forgotten, not because I've decided. Any shoulder-tip pain? Any time you actually fainted?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No shoulder pain. Yesterday when I got up the room spun for a second, dizzy, and then it was gone. I held the kitchen counter. I did not fall.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you taking these days?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Folic acid, once daily, after food. I think the tablet is 5 mg, maybe, I don't know, doctor. The strip is at home so I can't show you.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): And does once daily actually happen?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, no. Two days a week, sometimes three, I forget. Then I feel bad about it.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else, painkillers, hormone tablets?

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I took one Combiflam, only that one, day before yesterday, for the cramp. My sister said stop, so I stopped, I never took another. Meftal, which I used for period pain, I stopped it in March, not a single tablet since.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll note both as stopped. Did someone prescribe progesterone, Duphaston or similar?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): The clinic near my house wrote a white tablet. I never swallowed even one. The strip is unopened in the cupboard. I don't know the name and I won't guess.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it was never taken, it stays off the list. Any iron or vitamin you do take?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): At night, a red and black capsule. Pharmacy uncle said it is iron. I can't remember the brand, I'm sorry.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nameless iron capsule, night time, until we read the strip. Lie back, I want to feel your abdomen. Sandals can stay off, that's fine.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Sorry, the buckle sticks.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft. There is mild tenderness low down in the midline. No guarding, and no rebound. I am not doing an internal exam in clinic; the scan is the better test.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): So you can't tell me the baby is okay.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): I can't, and I won't pretend. Nausea, sleep, how is your mood in all this?

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): A little queasy in the morning, not terrible. Sleep is bad, I wake and check the liner again and again. And I'm anxious. When I think about it my heart races, like thudding.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's a miserable loop. Do you want your husband to come in?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes please. He's been waiting outside. He, um, he exaggerates, just so you know.
[SEG0039] person_1 (NURSE): I'll bring him.

[SEG0040] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, she is underplaying it. Bleeding is heavy, proper period type, and it has been going on since last week. Yesterday she nearly fainted in the kitchen, I caught her or she would have gone down.

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No. That is not what happened. It is spotting, not heavy, I already said brown drops. And I did not faint. You were in the hall, you didn't catch me. One second of dizziness, finished.
[SEG0042] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Last Sunday it started, so that is a week. In the night she was crying, holding her stomach, the pain was bad.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days or three days, not a week. I don't know why Sunday. And I was not crying. The cramp is mild, like a normal period. I was quiet because I was frightened, that's different.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm hearing two stories, so I'll say it back. Spotting duration sits somewhere between two or three days and about a week, not agreed. For how heavy, I am taking Priya's account, light spotting, not a period. The fainting he reports and she denies, I am not calling that established.
[SEG0045] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Also she vomits every morning. Chai doesn't stay, food doesn't stay. She has hardly eaten.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor, he is wrong. I have not vomited, not once. One morning I was queasy and I ate a smaller idli. I am eating.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vomiting stays disputed. I will not chart it as present and I will not pretend you agree. Let's leave the kitchen debate.
[SEG0048] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her mother had bleeding and lost the baby, she told me on the phone last night. So you can see why I am like this.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Aunt, not mother. And I don't actually know the story, it was years before I was born. He fills gaps.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then there is no clear family history for me to record. Surgeries, allergies, smoking, we are not opening all of that today. The scan is the priority.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I should say, I work in a bank, back-office, I took casual leave today. Just the two of us at home in Koramangala. And I left my tiffin in the car, of all things.
[SEG0052] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Curd rice. It'll keep, I'll bring it after.

[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Eat if you can, small portions, don't starve for this. No intercourse until the scan result is with us. No heavy lifting. You may walk about the house; I am not asking for strict bed rest, that old advice doesn't fix spotting.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): So no admission?
[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not from what I see. Today I'm booking a transvaginal scan, and bloods for serum beta-hCG, haemoglobin, and blood group with Rh. They should happen before you go home.
[SEG0056] person_1 (NURSE): Urine pregnancy test at check-in was positive, I have it on the slip. I can draw the blood in the side room whenever you say.

[SEG0057] person_3 (DOCTOR): A positive urine test confirms pregnancy hormone in the urine. It does not locate the pregnancy and it does not give the weeks. Please don't treat the slip as good news or bad news by itself.
[SEG0058] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): My mother will insist she lie flat till tomorrow.

[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tell her I disagreed. This part is strict, though. If the bleeding soaks a pad within an hour, or the pain becomes severe, or she faints, or shoulder pain or fever starts, come to emergency immediately, do not wait for the morning appointment.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): And if none of that happens?

[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back tomorrow morning, both of you, and we go through the scan and the hCG properly. No progesterone and no new tablet from me today. I don't want to treat a picture I haven't seen.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know how I'll sleep, doctor. My mind is very loud.

[SEG0063] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it gets too loud, call the hospital number printed on the slip, don't go down a search hole. Take the folic acid whenever you remember. Bring the red and black capsule tomorrow. Water in sips, and get up slowly.
[SEG0064] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Morning means what time? I have to message my manager.
[SEG0065] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ask reception for a morning slot, around nine if they have it. Nurse, can you send the bloods and fix this afternoon's scan?
[SEG0066] person_1 (NURSE): Scan is booked at half past two today. Priya, fist for me, we'll do the sample now. Small needle, I promise.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): I really hate needles. Um. Okay, okay, do it fast.
[SEG0068] person_1 (NURSE): Pinch, and done. Press on the cotton. You managed fine.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, about the dizziness. You still look worried.
[SEG0070] person_3 (DOCTOR): A brief spin on standing can be simple, but with early bleeding I want the scan before I reassure you. So not a clean all-clear on that, not yet.
[SEG0071] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She has barely had water. Half a glass since morning, I was watching.
[SEG0072] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not right. I had water and some buttermilk. Maybe less than usual, I don't know how many glasses. Not only half.
[SEG0073] person_3 (DOCTOR): Drink what sits comfortably, no heroics. I think we have covered the plan. Anything you still need to ask?
[SEG0074] person_2 (PATIENT): If the scan is bad, say it straight. I don't want gentle hints.
[SEG0075] person_3 (DOCTOR): Straight, tomorrow, looking at the pictures together. I won't guess in the corridor this afternoon.
[SEG0076] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thank you, doctor. We will come.
[SEG0077] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. Sorry, I really don't know the dates.
[SEG0078] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nothing to be sorry for. Ultrasound at half past two, and I'll see you tomorrow morning.
[SEG0079] person_1 (NURSE): Come, sit one minute, then I'll walk you to ultrasound. Husband, you can carry the bag.

spec.situation: Woman about 8-10 weeks pregnant with spotting and cramps; unsure of dates ('the last period was around Diwali, or after'); anxious; partner waits outside then joins. Scan and blood tests planned today, strict return advice.
features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

omissions.text: Folic acid dose is uncertain; the patient said she thinks it is 5 mg, maybe, and could not confirm because the strip was at home. Recording a definite 5 mg dose is incorrect.
Folic acid adherence detail is missing from the medication entry: she forgets it two days a week, sometimes three, rather than reliably taking it daily.
The patient reported no clots or tissue passed ('I don't think so. Just a few brown drops').
Internal pelvic examination was not performed in clinic; the doctor explicitly said he was not doing an internal exam and that the scan was the better test.
Vomiting should not be charted as present even with disputed certainty: the doctor explicitly said he would not chart vomiting as present because the patient denied it and the accounts did not agree.
No progesterone or any new tablet was prescribed today; doctor explicitly decided against starting progesterone or any new medication before seeing the scan.
A progesterone/white tablet had been prescribed by another clinic but was never taken; the strip is unopened and the patient did not know the name.
The doctor advised there was no need for admission based on current findings.

Emergency follow-up instruction was specifically to come to emergency immediately and not wait for the morning appointment if bleeding soaks a pad within an hour, pain becomes severe, she faints, or shoulder pain or fever starts.
The transvaginal scan was not just planned; it was booked for 2:30 pm the same day.
Follow-up timing was refined to ask reception for a morning slot around 9 am if available.
The doctor remained concerned enough about the brief dizziness that he would not give an all-clear until after the scan.
